description: Five-panel composite figure dominated by EBSD maps, with one TEM bright-field image; the group is mixed. Under the header "CR" (cold rolled), (a) is an EBSD phase map with a 10 µm scale bar showing alternating elongated dark bands labelled "deformed B2 stringer" and lighter regions labelled "deformed γ"; (b) is the parallel KAM map whose colour scale runs Min 0 to Max 5 (blue→green→yellow→red), rendering the γ bands dominantly red/green and the B2 stringers largely blue. Under the header "interrupted tensile, e = 0.05", (c) is a TEM bright-field image of sample "A15" (5 µm scale bar) with yellow arrow "deformed B2" and blue arrow "deformed γ", showing ellipsoidal B2 particles embedded in a deformed γ matrix, plus a lower-left inset of a single particle. (d) is the A15 EBSD phase map (1 µm scale bar) with teal B2 particles in a light γ matrix, red arrows at "γ-boundary" and a "deformed B2 stringer" label; (e) is its KAM map with white arrows marking "GND localization" along the γ/B2 interfaces. The figure argues that both γ and B2 co-deform, but strain and geometrically necessary dislocations localize preferentially in the softer γ and at γ/B2 interfaces.

subfigures.description: EBSD phase map of the cold-rolled (CR) condition, 10 µm scale bar; elongated dark bands labelled 'deformed B2 stringer' alternate with lighter regions labelled 'deformed γ', giving a banded two-phase structure.

EBSD KAM map parallel to (a), same field of view, colour scale Min 0 to Max 5; the deformed γ bands appear dominantly red/orange while the B2 stringer bands appear blue/green, indicating higher local misorientation (strain) in γ.

TEM bright-field image of sample 'A15' after interrupted tensile at e = 0.05, 5 µm scale bar; lenticular/ellipsoidal dark B2 particles sit in a deformed γ matrix (yellow arrow 'deformed B2', blue arrow 'deformed γ'), with a lower-left inset showing one particle at higher magnification.

EBSD phase map of A15 after interrupted tensile, 1 µm scale bar; teal rounded B2 particles (labelled 'B2') distributed in a light matrix labelled 'deformed γ', red arrows mark 'γ-boundary', and a 'deformed B2 stringer' label sits at the bottom.
EBSD KAM map matched to (d), Min 0/Max 5 colour scale; high-KAM (red/yellow) bands decorate the B2 particle perimeters and interfaces, with white arrows labelled 'GND localization'.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is an EBSD phase map of the cold-rolled (CR) sample with a 10 µm scale bar, showing a banded structure of elongated dark bands labelled 'deformed B2 stringer' alternating with lighter regions labelled 'deformed γ'.

Panel (b) is the KAM map corresponding to the same CR field as (a), and its colour scale is printed as Min 0 to Max 5; the deformed γ bands are rendered dominantly red whereas the B2 stringer bands remain largely blue/green.
The caption states that (a) is a phase map showing co-deformation of B2 stringer bands and γ, and (b) is a parallel KAM map showing strain localization in the respective phases during CR.

Panel (c) is a TEM bright-field image labelled 'A15' with a 5 µm scale bar, showing ellipsoidal dark B2 particles in a deformed matrix, annotated 'deformed B2' (yellow arrow) and 'deformed γ' (blue arrow), with an inset image at lower left.
The caption states that (c) shows deformed γ and B2 in A15 after an interrupted tensile test at plastic strain e = 0.05.

Panel (d) is an EBSD phase map of A15 after interrupted tensile (1 µm scale bar) in which rounded teal B2 particles are labelled 'B2' and lie in a light matrix labelled 'deformed γ'; red arrows annotate 'γ-boundary' and a 'deformed B2 stringer' label appears at the bottom.

Panel (e) is the A15 KAM map paired with (d), using the same Min 0/Max 5 colour scale, with white arrows labelled 'GND localization' pointing to high-misorientation regions at the B2 particle boundaries/γ–B2 interfaces.
The caption states that (d,e) show strain localization at the γ/B2 interface in A15 after interrupted tensile at e = 0.05.
The citing text states that because B2 is the harder phase, the strain concentration is higher in γ, which therefore deforms more (Figure 7b).
The citing text states that the TEM investigation of A15 after an interrupted tensile test at engineering strain = 0.05 found a higher dislocation density in γ than in B2 (Figure 7c).
The citing text states that dislocations released from softer γ localize around GB-B2 at the phase interfaces near γ grain boundaries (Figure 7d,e).
The citing text gives the bulk phase fractions of the alloy as 64% γ, 16% GB-B2 and 3.7% IG-B2, and states that γ/B2 strain incompatibility causes yield point elongation (YPE).
No numerical KAM values are printed on the maps other than the Min 0 / Max 5 endpoints of the colour bar; no axis or scale values beyond the 10 µm, 5 µm and 1 µm scale bars are given.
